free_tier.stated: Per-instance. Public table (read live) includes send.cyberjake.xyz at 10 GiB / 30 days / 100 downloads and send.adminforge.de at 8 GiB / 7 days / 1,000 downloads. The listed send.skylerszijjarto.com at 250 GiB / 7 days / 10,000 downloads and send.hostnetwork.xyz at 2.5 GiB / 999,999 downloads are the two outliers.

retention.stated: Retention: the Time limit column (3 to 30 days), MAX_EXPIRE_SECONDS on the server

egress.terms: unmetered; direct file URLs on the instance host, no egress pricing.

record.tooling: Ffsend (github.com/timvisee/ffsend). Real CLI with --host URL. Server is a self-hostable Rust binary, so the config (MAX_FILE_SIZE, MAX_EXPIRE_SECONDS) is public per instance.
record.chaining: 15+ public instances in the table, each an independent operator with its own quota => shard across instances rather than accounts. Since the server is self-hostable, the ceiling on an instance you run is only your own disk.

limits.value: Retention: the Time limit column (3 to 30 days
per-object-cap: the table's Size limit column (2.5 GiB

record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: the table's Size limit column (2.5 GiB to 250 GiB). Retention: the Time limit column (3 to 30 days), MAX_EXPIRE_SECONDS on the server. pull-count: the DL limit column. Adminforge allows 1,000, hostnetwork 999,999, but most sit at 10-100. The pull cap, not bytes, is the real bind on the E8 workload.
record.reliability_note: All files are E2E encrypted client-side and deleted on expiry; no originals re-encode.
